standard.name: Independent Bernoulli randomization at probability one half

assumptions.condition: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).

standard.name: Li--Wager independent unit-type and response sampling with uniform latent types

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

standard.name: Li--Wager bounded response and derivative envelope through order two
Known \(C^3\) radius separated from the lower-order response envelope

definitions.name: Li--Wager known-rank \(C^3\) class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius subclass of the Li--Wager sampling family selected by those properties; it is not a claim that the displayed class equals the full class used in LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Li--Wager finite indirect-effect benchmark
definitions.construction: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Exact realized-degree support correction
definitions.construction: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact symmetric discrete local-polynomial score
definitions.construction: For \(N_i>0\), let \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]\) and \(q_{i,h}=V_i\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}/\mu_{2,i}(h)\). For \(N_i=0\), set \(q_{i,h}=0\) and \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=0\).

definitions.name: Deterministically selected observed principal-component projector
definitions.construction:
Order the eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\) contain the first \(r\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
This deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map.

definitions.name: Explicit first-projection PC handle with bounded-difference certificate
Feasible explicit first-projection PC estimator
definitions.construction:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

definitions.name: Graph-observable degree-exact radii for the explicit PC handle
definitions.construction:
For the explicit certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), set
\[
 \overline b_h(A)=\frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
Thus \(\overline s_h(A)\) is a finite-sample conditional standard-deviation certificate, not an asserted sharp-rate formula.

definitions.name: Supported and degree-exact full-class envelopes
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}=\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\}\) and \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)]\).

definitions.name: Absolute-risk and honest-length criteria
definitions.construction: \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P(\theta_n\in\mathcal C)\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)]\), where the infima range over measurable procedures based on \((A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\).

statements.statement: For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i\ge1\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\). Symmetry of \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N_i,1/2)\) yields \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]=\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\). For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)|\le Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
statements.justification: This establishes exact derivative moments at every positive realized degree and removes the zero-normalizer failure at the lower bandwidth endpoint.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph uses an unlocalized global binomial score; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest does not face a random degree lattice.
statements.consumer: It supplies the unitwise bias and exact inverse-moment contribution in the feasible-PC certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i=N\geq1\), fix \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), and condition on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions.  By \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\),
\[
 M_i\mid A\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2),\qquad V_i=N^{-1}M_i-1/2.
\]
If \(N\) is even, the nearest nonzero lattice points are \(\pm N^{-1}\); if \(N\) is odd, they are \(\pm(2N)^{-1}\).  Each has positive binomial mass.  Thus \({\rm def:lattice-radius}\) implies
\[
 P\{0<|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\mid A\}>0,
\]
and \({\rm def:discrete-score}\) gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\).

The involution \(M_i\mapsto N-M_i\) preserves binomial mass and sends \(V_i\) to \(-V_i\).  The truncation indicator is even and the score is odd.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=1,
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^3\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]
 =\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]}{\mu_{2,i}(h)^2}
 =\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}.
\]

Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Taylor's formula at \(1/2\) and \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\) give
\[
 f_i(a,1/2+v)=f_i(a,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)v
 +\frac12\partial_x^2f_i(a,1/2)v^2+R_i(a,v),
 \qquad |R_i(a,v)|\leq \frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplication by \(q_{i,h}\), conditional expectation, and the three preceding moments yield
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A].
\]
On the support of the score, \(|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\), whence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}R_i(a,V_i)\mid A]\right|
 &\leq \frac{L}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[|V_i|^4\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]\\
 &\leq \frac{Lh_i(h)^2}{6\mu_{2,i}(h)}
 \mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf1\{|V_i|\leq h_i(h)\}\mid A]
 =\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every division is justified by the strict positivity already proved.

statements.statement: Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the new derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy \( |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|\le L(8n)^{-1}\sum_{i:N_i>0}N_i^{-1}+Bn^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}\). Consequently, in the degree regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6, this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\), so their Gaussian theorem is an asymptotic benchmark for \(\theta_n\), not a finite-sample same-target result.
statements.justification: The bridge states exactly when the published finite indirect effect and the finite-population derivative are asymptotically interchangeable.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition 1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets.
statements.consumer: It permits valid asymptotic comparison with Theorem 6 while keeping the proposed finite-population derivative as a distinct target.
statements.proof_tex:
Work first conditionally on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\).  For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\), define the proof-intermediate function
\[
g_i(x):=\frac{f_i(1,x)+f_i(0,x)}{2},\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
Fix \(i\) with \(N_i=m>0\).  By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-design}\), conditional on \(A\) and all preassignment variables, \(M_i\sim {\rm Binomial}(m,1/2)\), and \(Z_i\) is independent of \(M_i\).  The conditional assignment law does not depend on the latent types, so the same assertions hold after conditioning only on \(A\) and \((f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\), by iterated conditional expectation.  Hence \(\texttt{ass:anonymous-interference}\) and \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\) give the unit-level contribution
\[
\begin{aligned}
\beta_i
&:=4\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[Y_i(Z)(M_i-m/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right]\\
&=4m\,\mathbb E_Z\!\left[g_i(1/2+V_i)V_i\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(m=0\), then \(M_i-N_i/2=0\), so the same definition gives \(\beta_i=0\).  Consequently,
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_i.
\]

For \(m>0\), let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent variables taking the values \(-1/2\) and \(1/2\) with equal probability, and put \(S_m=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j\).  Conditionally on the quantities fixed above, \(V_i\) has the law of \(S_m/m\).  Independence and centering, together with \(\mathbb E X_j^2=1/4\) and \(\mathbb E X_j^4=1/16\), yield
\[
\mathbb E S_m^2=\frac m4,
\qquad
\mathbb E S_m^3=0,
\]
and, because only the one-index and two-pair terms survive in the fourth-power expansion,
\[
\mathbb E S_m^4
=\sum_{j=1}^m\mathbb E X_j^4
+6\sum_{1\le j<k\le m}\mathbb E X_j^2\mathbb E X_k^2
=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathbb E V_i=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^2=\frac1{4m},
\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^3=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E V_i^4=\frac{3m^2-2m}{16m^4}\le\frac3{16m^2}.
\]

By \(\texttt{ass:third-derivative-bound}\), the averaging defining \(g_i\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|g_i^{(3)}(x)|\le L.
\]
Repeated integration of \(g_i^{(3)}\) along the segment from \(1/2\) to \(1/2+v\), which lies in \([0,1]\) for every realized \(v=V_i\), gives
\[
g_i(1/2+v)
=g_i(1/2)+g_i'(1/2)v+\frac12g_i''(1/2)v^2+R_i(v),
\qquad
|R_i(v)|\le\frac L6|v|^3.
\]
Multiplying by \(v\), taking conditional expectations, and using the four moment identities shows that the constant and quadratic terms vanish, while \(4m\mathbb E V_i^2=1\).  Hence
\[
\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)
=4m\,\mathbb E\!\left[V_iR_i(V_i)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}\right],
\]
and thus
\[
|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
\le \frac{4mL}{6}\mathbb E V_i^4
\le \frac{4mL}{6}\frac3{16m^2}
=\frac{L}{8m}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:target}\), the contribution of unit \(i\) to \(\theta_n\) is \(g_i'(1/2)\).  If \(N_i=0\), then \(\texttt{ass:response-envelope}\) implies
\[
|g_i'(1/2)|
\le\frac{|\partial_x f_i(1,1/2)|+|\partial_x f_i(0,1/2)|}{2}
\le B.
\]
Separating nonisolated and isolated vertices and applying the triangle inequality now proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|
&\le \frac1n\sum_{i:N_i>0}|\beta_i-g_i'(1/2)|
+\frac1n\sum_{i:N_i=0}|g_i'(1/2)|\\
&\le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}
+\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to establish the asserted asymptotic comparison.  Consider a triangular-array sequence in the Li--Wager Theorem~6 regime, hence satisfying all hypotheses of that theorem.  The uniform latent-type marginal is the one recorded in the repaired Li--Wager sampling condition \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\), and \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\) gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log\rho_n}{\log n}>-\frac12.
\]
Choose \(\varepsilon>0\) strictly smaller than the gap between this lower limit and \(-1/2\).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\rho_n\ge n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.
\]
By the independence and uniform marginal in \(\texttt{ass:unit-sampling}\), and the conditional edge independence in \(\texttt{ass:graphon-draw}\), the pairs governing edges incident to \(i\) are independent after conditioning on \(U_i=u\).  Thus
\[
N_i\mid U_i=u\sim {\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n(u)),
\qquad
p_n(u)=\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv.
\]
The displayed parameter belongs to \([0,1]\) by \(\texttt{ass:edge-probability}\) and \(\texttt{ass:kernel-bound}\).  By \(\texttt{ass:degree-regularity}\), for Lebesgue-almost every \(u\),
\[
\mu_i(u):=\mathbb E[N_i\mid U_i=u]
=(n-1)p_n(u)
\ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}.
\]
Because every \(U_i\) is uniform, all realized latent types lie in this full-measure set almost surely.

We derive the required lower-tail estimate directly.  If \(S\sim{\rm Binomial}(m,p)\), \(\mu=mp\), and \(t=\log2\), exponential Markov's inequality and \(1-y\le e^{-y}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P(S\le\mu/2)
&\le e^{t\mu/2}\mathbb E e^{-tS}
=e^{t\mu/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^m\\
&\le\exp\!\left\{\frac{t\mu}{2}-\mu(1-e^{-t})\right\}
=\exp\!\left\{-\frac{1-\log2}{2}\mu\right\}
\le e^{-\mu/8},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last inequality uses \((1-\log2)/2\ge1/8\).  Apply this estimate conditionally on each \(U_i\), use the preceding lower bound for \(\mu_i(U_i)\), and take a union bound.  For
\[
\mathcal E_n
:=\left\{\min_{i\in\mathcal V_n}N_i\ge\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{2\kappa}\right\},
\]
we obtain
\[
\mathbb P(\mathcal E_n^c)
\le n\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{8\kappa}\right\}
\longrightarrow0,
\]
because \(n\rho_n\ge n^{1/2+\varepsilon}\) eventually.  On \(\mathcal E_n\) there are no isolates, and the finite-sample inequality already proved yields
\[
\frac{|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n|}{\sqrt{\rho_n}}
\le\frac{L\kappa}{4(n-1)\rho_n^{3/2}}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(n-1)\rho_n^{3/2}
\ge(1-o(1))n^{1/4+3\varepsilon/2}
\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The radii \(L\) and \(\kappa\) are fixed class constants.  Combining the last three displays proves
\[
\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n}).
\]
Finally, \(\texttt{lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\) records that the published PC-balancing Gaussian limit is centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) on the same \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale.  The last display therefore makes that result an asymptotic benchmark for \(\theta_n\) along every nondegenerate sequence satisfying all of Theorem~6's hypotheses.  The finite-sample functionals remain distinct by \(\texttt{def:target}\) and \(\texttt{def:li-wager-target}\), exactly as the degree-exact inequality records.

statements.statement:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), let \(h=h^\dagger\).  The feasible estimator and interval in \({\rm def:estimator}\) and \({\rm def:honest-interval}\) satisfy \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|\le\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}\ge1-\alpha\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]
 \le2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Before intersection with \([-B,B]\), the pointwise half-length is exactly \(\overline b_{h^\dagger}(A)+\overline s_{h^\dagger}(A)/\sqrt\alpha\), including every realized degree and isolate.  No comparison of \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) with \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is asserted.
statements.justification: This theorem gives exact finite-sample risk, coverage, and expected-length inequalities in terms of the observable radius envelope.
statements.gap: No theorem compares the conservative observable envelope with the analytic supported envelope, so this is not a sharp rate result.
statements.consumer: Experimenters can report the realized interval safely and treat a wide certificate as evidence for an ego-cluster follow-up.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), and put
\[
 \mathcal G=\sigma\!\left(A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\right),
 \qquad E_h=\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n,
 \qquad m_h=\mathbb E_P(E_h\mid\mathcal G).
\tag{21}
\]
The objective in \({\rm def:exact-optimal-bandwidth}\) has a minimizer.  Across all possible degrees, the score and every finite-lattice certificate in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) have finitely many bandwidth breakpoints.  On each interval beginning at one such included breakpoint, the stochastic and PC-bias certificates are constant and the Taylor part is continuous and nondecreasing.  The supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) remains nondecreasing there, so its minimum on that interval is attained at the included left endpoint.  Since \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\) is a nonempty compact interval and there are finitely many endpoints, a global minimum is attained.  Thus the smallest minimizer \(h^\dagger\) is well defined and depends on the class, not on the observed sample.

By \({\rm thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate}\),
\[
 |m_h|\le\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\{(E_h-m_h)^2\mid\mathcal G\}
 \le\overline s_h(A)^2.
\tag{22}
\]
Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and (22) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P(|E_h|\mid\mathcal G)
 \le |m_h|+\{\mathbb E_P((E_h-m_h)^2\mid\mathcal G)\}^{1/2}
 \le\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A).
\tag{23}
\]
Taking expectations, setting \(h=h^\dagger\), taking the supremum over the model class, and applying \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\) proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{h^\dagger}-\theta_n|
 \le\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{24}
\]

Conditional Chebyshev applied to (22) gives
\[
 P\!\left(
 |E_h-m_h|>\overline s_h(A)/\sqrt\alpha
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal G\right)\le\alpha;
\tag{25}
\]
when \(\overline s_h(A)=0\), (22) makes the left side zero.  The triangle inequality and the bias part of (22) turn (25) into coverage by the untruncated interval.  Moreover, \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) and \({\rm def:target}\) give \(|\theta_n|\le B\), so intersection with \([-B,B]\) cannot remove \(\theta_n\).  Integrating and setting \(h=h^\dagger\) proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{h^\dagger}\}
 \ge1-\alpha.
\tag{26}
\]

Before intersection with \([-B,B]\), \({\rm def:honest-interval}\) has half-length exactly \(\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)/\sqrt\alpha\).  Intersection only shortens it, and hence
\[
 \operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_h)
 \le2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}
 \{\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\}.
\tag{27}
\]
Expectation, the class supremum, \(h=h^\dagger\), and \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\) now yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{h^\dagger})]
 \le2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{28}
\]
The finite degree-lattice quantities in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) and the isolate summand in \({\rm def:radii}\) show that the certificate includes every realized degree and isolate.  Equations (24), (26), and (28) prove the proposed statement.  None compares \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\) to \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\).

statements.statement:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  The two displayed compatibility inequalities are only sufficient conditions for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same supported lower benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.

statements.proof_tex:
\textit{Step 1: the compatible block submodel.}
Let \(U_i\) be i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]\), use the cells, functions, and kernel displayed in the statement, and write \(T_0\) for the integral operator with kernel \(W_0\).  The intervals form a partition up to null endpoints.  Hence, for all \(1\leq k,\ell\leq r\),
\[
 \int_0^1\psi_k(u)\psi_\ell(u)\,du
 =r\,|I_k\cap I_\ell|=\mathbf 1\{k=\ell\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 (T_0\psi_k)(u)
 =c_0\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\int_{I_k}\sqrt r\,dv
 =\frac{c_0}{r}\psi_k(u).
\tag{2}
\]
The ranges of the \(r\) functions in (1) span the range of \(T_0\), so (2) proves that \(W_0\) has exact rank \(r\) and that every nonzero eigenvalue equals \(c_0/r\).  By the definition of \(c_0\),
\[
 \frac{c_0}{r}\geq\underline\lambda,
 \qquad
 \int_0^1W_0(u,v)\,dv=\frac{c_0}{r}\geq\kappa^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
The local condition \(c_0\leq\kappa\) gives \(0\leq W_0\leq\kappa\).  Together with \({\rm ass:edge\text{-}probability}\), it also gives
\[
 0\leq\rho_nW_0(u,v)\leq\rho_n\kappa\leq1,
\tag{4}
\]
so all Bernoulli edge probabilities are valid.

For completeness, we write out the Bernstein condition used in \({\rm ass:eigenfunction\text{-}bernstein}\): for a centered variable \(X\), it is
\[
 \mathbb E|X|^q\leq\frac{q!}{2}\mathbb E[X^2]b_\psi^{q-2},
 \qquad q\geq2.
\tag{5}
\]
Here \(\mathbb E\psi_k(U_i)=r^{-1/2}\).  If \(r\geq2\), then
\[
 \left|\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right|
 \leq\frac{r-1}{\sqrt r}\leq b_\psi.
\tag{6}
\]
Consequently, raising the bound in (6) to the power \(q-2\), multiplying by the square, and taking expectations gives
\[
 \mathbb E\left|\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right|^q
 \leq b_\psi^{q-2}\mathbb E\left[\left\{\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right\}^2\right]
 \leq\frac{q!}{2}b_\psi^{q-2}\mathbb E\left[\left\{\psi_k(U_i)-r^{-1/2}\right\}^2\right].
\tag{7}
\]
For \(r=1\) the centered variable is zero, so (5) is immediate.  Equations (1)--(7) verify orthonormality, exact rank, spectral strength, kernel bounds, row-mass regularity, the Bernstein moment condition, and edge-probability feasibility.  The i.i.d. latent types, the graph drawn conditionally according to \(W_0\), and the independent Bernoulli assignment then satisfy \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\), \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\), and \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\).

Set \(s_0=B/4\) and let the i.i.d. intercepts \(\xi_i\), independent of all graph and assignment variables, have density
\[
p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}p_{s_0}(t)\,dt
 =s_0^{-1}\int_{-s_0}^{s_0}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)dt=1.
\]
For any deterministic \(g\in C^3[0,1]\), define the two response laws by
\[
 f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x),
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in[0,1].
\tag{9}
\]
Every construction below chooses \(g\) so that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq3B/4,
 \quad \|g'\|_\infty\leq B,
 \quad \|g''\|_\infty\leq B,
 \quad \|g'''\|_\infty\leq L.
\tag{10}
\]
Since \(|\xi_i|\leq B/4\), (10) verifies \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and \({\rm ass:third\text{-}derivative\text{-}bound}\); (9) verifies anonymous interference when inserted in \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\).  Thus, after (10) is checked separately for each \(g\), the induced laws are members of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), rather than merely oracle experiments outside the model.

Under (9), the target in \({\rm def:target}\) is nonrandom and equals
\[
 \theta_n^\pm=\pm g'(1/2),
 \qquad
 \Delta_g:=|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=2|g'(1/2)|.
\tag{11}
\]

\textit{Step 2: a common experiment-distance inequality.}
Let \(q_{s_0}=\sqrt{p_{s_0}}\).  The function \(q_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1/2}\cos(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\) is absolutely continuous after extension by zero, because it vanishes at both endpoints.  Its weak derivative satisfies
\[
 \|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2
 =\frac1{s_0}\left(\frac{\pi}{2s_0}\right)^2
 \int_{-s_0}^{s_0}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)dt
 =\frac{\pi^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{12}
\]
The fundamental theorem of calculus followed by Minkowski's integral inequality therefore yields, for every \(\eta_1,\eta_2\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 H^2\{p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1),p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\}
 =\|q_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1)-q_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\|_2^2
 \leq(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2\|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2
 =\frac{\pi^2(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{13}
\]
We use the convention in (13) for squared Hellinger distance.  Conditional on \((A,Z)\), the responses are independent translated intercepts.  If \(Q_g^+\) and \(Q_g^-\) denote the two observed-data laws, the product-affinity identity and \(1-\prod_i(1-x_i)\leq\sum_i x_i\) give, from (13) with translations differing by \(2g(X_i)\),
\[
 H^2(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{s_0^2}\mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^ng(X_i)^2,
 \qquad
 X_i=\begin{cases}1/2+V_i,&N_i>0,\\0,&N_i=0.\end{cases}
\tag{14}
\]
The outer expectation in (14) is valid because the law of \((A,Z)\) is identical in the two experiments.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq H(Q_g^+,Q_g^-).
\tag{15}
\]

\textit{Step 3: the linear graph-floor pair.}
Put \(\bar c=c_0/r\).  Conditional on \(U_i\), each other unit belongs to the same block with probability \(1/r\), independently, and the edge is then present with probability \(\rho_nc_0\).  Thus
\[
 N_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n),
 \qquad p_n=\frac{c_0d}{rn}=\frac{\bar c d}{n},
 \qquad \mu_n:=(n-1)p_n\asymp d.
\tag{16}
\]
Conditional on \(N_i=N>0\), Bernoulli randomization gives \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\), whence
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mid A,N_i=N]=\frac1{4N}.
\tag{17}
\]
For a binomial variable with \(n-1\) trials,
\[
 \mathbb E\frac1{N_i+1}
 =\frac{1-(1-p_n)^n}{np_n}\leq\frac1{np_n}.
\tag{18}
\]
Since \(N^{-1}\leq2(N+1)^{-1}\) for \(N\geq1\), (17)--(18) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^nV_i^2\mathbf 1\{N_i>0\}
 =\frac n4\mathbb E\{N_i^{-1}\mathbf 1(N_i>0)\}
 \leq\frac{n}{2np_n}=O(n/d).
\tag{19}
\]
Also,
\[
 n\Pr(N_i=0)=n(1-p_n)^{n-1}
 \leq n e^{-\mu_n}=O(ne^{-c d})
\tag{20}
\]
for a constant \(c>0\) depending only on the fixed block parameters.

Take
\[
 g_G(x)=c_GB\sqrt{d/n}\,(x-1/2).
\tag{21}
\]
Because \(d/n\to0\), choosing \(c_G\leq1\) verifies all four inequalities in (10) for large \(n\).  By (19)--(21),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\sum_i g_G(X_i)^2
 &=c_G^2B^2\frac dn
 \left\{\mathbb E\sum_iV_i^2\mathbf 1(N_i>0)
       +\frac n4\Pr(N_i=0)\right\}\\
 &\leq Cc_G^2B^2\{1+d e^{-cd}\}\leq C'c_G^2B^2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{22}
\]
Since \(s_0=B/4\), (14)--(15) and (22) show that \(c_G>0\) may be chosen, independently of \(n,d\), so that
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_G^+,Q_G^-)\leq\eta,
 \qquad \eta:=(1-2\alpha)/2>0.
\tag{23}
\]
By (11) and (21), this pair has separation
\[
 \Delta_G=2c_GB\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{24}
\]

\textit{Step 4: the interior nonlinear bump.}
Fix the explicit odd function
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-4t^2)^4\mathbf 1\{|t|<1/2\}.
\tag{25}
\]
Its derivatives through order three match zero at \(\{-1/2,1/2\}\), so \(\phi\in C^3(\mathbb R)\), its support lies strictly inside \((-1,1)\), and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  For \(0\leq j_0\leq3\), let \(C_{j_0}=\|\phi^{(j_0)}\|_\infty<\infty\).  For \(d^{-1}\leq h\leq d^{-1/2}\), set
\[
 g_h(x)=c_ILh^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{h}\right).
\tag{26}
\]
Then
\[
 \|g_h^{(j_0)}\|_\infty=c_ILh^{3-j_0}C_{j_0},
 \qquad 0\leq j_0\leq3.
\tag{27}
\]
Choose \(c_I C_3\leq1\).  Since \(d\geq C_{\log}\log n\) implies \(h\leq d^{-1/2}\to0\), (27) verifies (10) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(B,L\).

We next prove the local binomial-mass bound used in (14).  For \(N\geq1\), the largest atom of \({\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\) is at most \(C/\sqrt N\).  Indeed, for \(N=2q_0\), if \(a_{q_0}={2q_0\choose q_0}4^{-q_0}\), then \(a_0=1\),
\[
 \frac{a_{q_0+1}}{a_{q_0}}=\frac{2q_0+1}{2q_0+2},
 \qquad
 \left(\frac{2q_0+1}{2q_0+2}\right)^2\leq\frac{q_0+1}{q_0+2},
\tag{28}
\]
so induction gives \(a_{q_0}\leq(q_0+1)^{-1/2}\); the odd case is bounded by the preceding even case.  The interval \(|M/N-1/2|\leq h\) contains at most \(2Nh+2\) integers.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr\{|M/N-1/2|\leq h\mid N\}
 \leq C(\sqrt N h+N^{-1/2}).
\tag{29}
\]
For \(N_i\) in (16), exponential Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{-tN_i}\) with \(t=\log2\) gives \(\Pr(N_i<\mu_n/2)\leq e^{-\mu_n/8}\).  Jensen's inequality and a split at \(\mu_n/2\) then give
\[
 \mathbb E\sqrt{N_i}\leq\sqrt{\mu_n},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\{N_i^{-1/2}\mathbf 1(N_i>0)\}
 \leq\sqrt{2/\mu_n}+e^{-\mu_n/8}.
\tag{30}
\]
Combining (29)--(30), using \(\mu_n\asymp d\) and \(h\geq d^{-1}\), yields the uniform bound
\[
 \Pr(|V_i|\leq h,N_i>0)\leq C\sqrt d\,h.
\tag{31}
\]
The bump is zero for isolates and outside the event in (31).  Hence (14), (26), and (31) imply
\[
 H^2(Q_h^+,Q_h^-)
 \leq Cc_I^2n\sqrt d\,L^2h^7.
\tag{32}
\]
For \(L>0\), define the proof-intermediate bandwidth
\[
 h_0=\left(\frac{L^{-2}}{n\sqrt d}\right)^{1/7}.
\tag{33}
\]
When \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), substituting \(h=h_0\) in (32) leaves the right-hand side bounded by \(Cc_I^2\).  Decreasing \(c_I\), if necessary, makes the total variation at most \(\eta\).  Equations (11), (26), and (33) give
\[
 \Delta_I=2c_ILh_0^2
 =2c_IL^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{34}
\]

\textit{Step 5: the invisible degree-lattice bump.}
Let \(D_n=\lceil Kd\rceil\), where \(K>e\bar c\) is fixed sufficiently large.  For \(t>0\), exponential Markov's inequality and \(1+y\leq e^y\) give
\[
 \Pr(N_i>D_n)
 \leq e^{-tD_n}(1-p_n+p_ne^t)^{n-1}
 \leq\exp\{-tD_n+\mu_n(e^t-1)\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\log(D_n/\mu_n)\) when \(D_n\geq\mu_n\) yields
\[
 \Pr(N_i>D_n)\leq\left(\frac{e\mu_n}{D_n}\right)^{D_n}
 \leq e^{-a_Kd}.
\tag{35}
\]
Choose \(K\) so large that \(a_KC_{\log}>2\).  The union bound and \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\) give
\[
 \Pr\left(\max_iN_i>D_n\right)
 \leq ne^{-a_Kd}=o(1).
\tag{36}
\]
Put \(w_n=(4D_n)^{-1}\) and
\[
 g_D(x)=c_D Lw_n^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{w_n}\right),
\tag{37}
\]
where \(c_DC_3\leq1\).  The analogue of (27), together with \(D_n\to\infty\), verifies (10) for large \(n\).  If \(1\leq N_i\leq D_n\), every noncentral point of the exposure lattice has
\[
 |V_i|\geq\begin{cases}N_i^{-1},&N_i\text{ even},\\(2N_i)^{-1},&N_i\text{ odd},\end{cases}
 \geq(2D_n)^{-1}>w_n.
\tag{38}
\]
At the central point \(V_i=0\), oddness gives \(g_D(1/2)=0\); for an isolate, \(g_D(0)=0\).  Thus on \(E_n=\{\max_iN_i\leq D_n\}\), every observed response equals \(\xi_i\) under both signs.  The restrictions of the two observed laws to \(E_n\) are identical, and (36) consequently implies
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_D^+,Q_D^-)
 \leq\Pr(E_n^c)=o(1).
\tag{39}
\]
On the other hand, (11) and (37) give
\[
 \Delta_D=2c_D Lw_n^2\asymp Ld^{-2}.
\tag{40}
\]
This proves invisibility from the actual lattice, rather than putting that property into the construction by definition.

\textit{Step 6: risk and honest-length reductions.}
Consider any one of the three pairs above and abbreviate its targets by \(\theta^+,\theta^-\), its observed laws by \(Q^+,Q^-\), and its separation by \(\Delta\).  For an arbitrary estimator \(T\), let \(A_T=\{|T-\theta^+|\geq\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_T^c\), the triangle inequality gives \(|T-\theta^-|\geq\Delta/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}|T-\theta^+|+\mathbb E_{Q^-}|T-\theta^-|
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{Q^+(A_T)+Q^-(A_T^c)\}\\
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{41}
\]
Thus the larger of the two risks is at least \(\Delta\{1-\operatorname{TV}\}/4\).

Now let \(\mathcal C\) be any confidence interval having coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under every member of the class.  Total variation and the union bound imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q^+\{\theta^+,\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}
 &\geq Q^+\{\theta^+\in\mathcal C\}
       +Q^+\{\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}-1\\
 &\geq(1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-))-1\\
 &=1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{42}
\]
An interval containing both target values has length at least \(\Delta\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)
 \geq\Delta\{1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
\tag{43}
\]
By (23), (32)--(34), and (39), all pairwise total variations are eventually at most \(\eta=(1-2\alpha)/2\).  Equations (41) and (43), followed by the infima in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\), therefore yield the lower orders in (24), (34), and (40) for both \(R^*_{n,d,L}\) and \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\).

\textit{Step 7: comparison with the bandwidth envelope.}
Write \(a_n=(n\sqrt d)^{-1/2}\).  For \(L>0\), (33) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2=a_nh_0^{-3/2}=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{44}
\]
If \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), evaluate the infimum in \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\) at \(h=d^{-1}\).  The condition \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\) is equivalent to \(L^2\geq d^{13/2}/n\), and hence
\[
 a_nd^{3/2}=d^{5/4}n^{-1/2}\leq Ld^{-2},
 \qquad
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{45}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), evaluation at \(h_0\), using (44), gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{46}
\]
If \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\), then \(L^2\leq d^3/n\).  Evaluation at \(h=d^{-1/2}\) gives
\[
 Ld^{-1}\leq\sqrt{d/n},
 \qquad
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{47}
\]
For \(L=0\), the infimum is attained at \(d^{-1/2}\) and equals \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  In the first regime, combine the graph pair (24) and lattice pair (40); in the second, combine (24) and (34); and in the third and in the case \(L=0\), use (24).  Since \(\max\{x,y\}\geq(x+y)/2\), (45)--(47) show that both minimax criteria are bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of
\[
 \sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \left\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\right\}
 =\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\tag{48}
\]
All constants used to make the experiment distances small depend only on the fixed class constants and \(\alpha\), not on \(n,d\).  This completes the conditional block-submodel converse and does not extend it beyond the two sufficient compatibility inequalities in the statement.

statements.statement:
For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), the explicit degree-exact procedure proves
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the repaired class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  No bound \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is proved; hence the three analytic phases are a tuning geometry and a minimax lower benchmark, not an achieved honest expected-length frontier.
statements.justification: This proposition proves the bandwidth optimization and the honest lower--upper bracket without calling the conservative upper envelope sharp.
statements.gap: The bounded-difference certificate has no proved comparison with the analytic supported envelope, so tightness of the displayed bracket remains unresolved.
statements.consumer: The three phases are useful for design triage as lower-benchmark geometry, not as a guaranteed confidence-length curve.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(L>0\), and write
\[
 c_{n,d}=n^{-1/2}d^{-1/4},
 \qquad
 g(h)=Lh^2+c_{n,d}h^{-3/2},
 \qquad
 \ell=d^{-1},
 \qquad
 u=d^{-1/2}.
\tag{64}
\]
By \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\), \(d\to\infty\), so at every sufficiently large index \(d\geq4\) and \({\rm def:bandwidth\text{-}set}\) gives \(\mathcal H_{n,d}=[\ell,u]\).  From \({\rm def:optimal\text{-}bandwidth}\),
\[
 h_0^7=\frac{L^{-2}}{n\sqrt d}.
\tag{65}
\]
Since \(c_{n,d}^2=(n\sqrt d)^{-1}\), positive square roots in (65) give
\[
 Lh_0^2=c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}.
\tag{66}
\]

If \(h_0\leq\ell\), then \(g(h)\geq L\ell^2\) for every \(h\in[\ell,u]\), while monotonicity and (66) give
\[
 c_{n,d}\ell^{-3/2}
 \leq c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}
 =Lh_0^2\leq L\ell^2.
\tag{67}
\]
Evaluation at \(\ell\) proves
\[
 Ld^{-2}\leq\inf_{h\in[\ell,u]}g(h)\leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{68}
\]
If \(\ell<h_0<u\), then for \(h\geq h_0\) the first term of \(g(h)\) is at least \(Lh_0^2\), and for \(h\leq h_0\) its second term is at least \(c_{n,d}h_0^{-3/2}=Lh_0^2\).  Evaluation at \(h_0\) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2\leq\inf_{h\in[\ell,u]}g(h)\leq2Lh_0^2,
 \qquad
 Lh_0^2=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{69}
\]
If \(h_0\geq u\), then
\[
 g(h)\geq c_{n,d}u^{-3/2}=\sqrt{d/n}
\tag{70}
\]
for every admissible \(h\), while (66) and \(u\leq h_0\) imply \(Lu^2\leq c_{n,d}u^{-3/2}\).  Evaluation at \(u\) yields
\[
 \sqrt{d/n}\leq\inf_{h\in[\ell,u]}g(h)\leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{71}
\]
By \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\),
\[
 \mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 =\sqrt{d/n}+\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}g(h).
\tag{72}
\]
Adding \(\sqrt{d/n}\) to (68)--(71) proves the three asserted analytic equivalences.

At every index with nonempty bandwidth set, \({\rm thm:honest\text{-}upper}\) supplies a measurable estimator with worst-case absolute risk at most \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\), and an interval meeting the uniform coverage constraint with worst-case expected length at most \(2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\).  Inserting these procedures into the infima in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\) gives
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{73}
\]
Along every sequence satisfying the hypotheses of \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\), that theorem, now proved while retaining the independent uniform latent types and the original admissible kernel, gives a constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
\tag{74}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Finally, \({\rm thm:conditional\text{-}isolate\text{-}wall}\) proves pointwise that every graph-only conditional-bias radius over the same class satisfies
\[
 b(A)\geq\frac Bn\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\tag{75}
\]
Equations (68)--(75) prove the analytic phases and the honest bracket
\[
 c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 \leq R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}
 \leq\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\max\{1,\alpha^{-1/2}\}\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\tag{76}
\]
Neither \({\rm def:radii}\) nor \({\rm thm:honest\text{-}upper}\) supplies \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\).  Therefore the three phases are a tuning geometry and minimax lower benchmark, not an achieved honest expected-length frontier, exactly as asserted.

statements.statement:
On the predeclared sharp-radius class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\subseteq\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), evaluate \({\rm def:radii}\) and \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\) at \(L=0\).  Then \(h_0=\infty\), \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), and the positive-degree Taylor term in \(\overline b_{h_\star}(A)\) is identically zero.  The exact moment equation \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\) also cancels every quadratic exposure response, with affine responses as a special case.  At \(h_\star=d^{-1/2}\), the analytic nonremainder score and graph terms both have order \(\sqrt{d/n}\), while the complete corrected certificate is
\[
 \overline b_{h_\star}(A)=\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star},
 \qquad
 \overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_{ij,h_\star}\right)^2.
\]
No sharp stochastic order is asserted for the last display.  An affine realized law inside \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) with \(L>0\) does not permit setting the honesty radius to zero; the reduction applies only when \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\) is fixed before observing the experiment.
statements.justification: On the prespecified zero-radius class, every exposure response is quadratic and the exact discrete moments eliminate its positive-degree approximation error.
statements.gap: The corrected bounded-difference variance radius remains explicit but has no sharp stochastic order, even in this zero-radius reduction.
statements.consumer: Analysts may use the largest admissible bandwidth only when the zero-radius class was fixed before outcomes were observed.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a law in the prespecified class \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\).  By \({\rm ass:third-derivative-bound}\) with radius zero,
\[
 \sup_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\sup_{a\in\{0,1\},\,x\in[0,1]}
 |\partial_x^3 f_i(a,x)|\le0,
\]
and hence \(\partial_x^3f_i(a,x)=0\) for every displayed argument.  Since each response is \(C^3\), for \(x,y\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \partial_x^2f_i(a,x)-\partial_x^2f_i(a,y)
 =\int_y^x\partial_t^3f_i(a,t)\,dt=0.
\]
Thus the second derivative is constant, and integrating twice shows that \(x\mapsto f_i(a,x)\) is a polynomial of degree at most two.

Substitution of \(L=0\) into \({\rm def:optimal-bandwidth}\) gives \(h_0=\infty\) and
\[
 h_\star=\min\{d^{-1/2},\max\{d^{-1},\infty\}\}=d^{-1/2}.
\tag{37}
\]
The logarithmic-degree condition in \({\rm def:model-class}\) implies \(d\ge4\) at all sufficiently large indices, so \(d^{-1}\le d^{-1/2}\le1/2\), and (37) belongs to \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\) by \({\rm def:bandwidth-set}\).  The positive-degree Taylor term in \({\rm def:radii}\) is multiplied by \(L\), and is therefore zero.

Fix \(i\) with \(N_i>0\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  By \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\), exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\) and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0,
 \quad
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1,
 \quad
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0.
\tag{38}
\]
The exact quadratic expansion is
\[
 f_i(a,1/2+V_i)
 =f_i(a,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)V_i
 +\frac12\partial_x^2f_i(a,1/2)V_i^2.
\]
Multiplication by \(q_{i,h}\), conditional expectation, and (38) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]
 =\partial_xf_i(a,1/2).
\tag{39}
\]
Thus every quadratic response, including every affine response, has zero positive-degree approximation error.

At (37), the analytic stochastic term in \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\) is
\[
 (n\sqrt d\,h_\star^3)^{-1/2}
 =(n\sqrt d\,d^{-3/2})^{-1/2}=\sqrt{d/n},
\tag{40}
\]
and the graph term is also \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  Direct substitution of \(L=0\), \(h=h_\star\), the corrected \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), and the corrected \({\rm def:radii}\) gives
\[
 \overline b_{h_\star}(A)
 =\frac Bn\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}
\tag{41}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_{h_\star}(A)^2
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h_\star}
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\beta_{ij,h_\star}\right)^2.
\tag{42}
\]
The certification in \({\rm thm:explicit-pc-conditional-certificate}\) proves that (41)--(42) are the complete conditional certificates.  No stochastic order for (42) has been used.

All member properties other than the third-derivative radius are identical at radii zero and \(L\), so \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\subseteq\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  To see why a realized affine response does not permit a post hoc radius-zero analysis when \(L>0\), retain the graph and uniform latent-type law of any admissible member and replace its response draw by the deterministic function
\[
 g(a,x)=c(x-1/2)^3,
 \qquad c=\frac12\min\{B/3,L/6\}>0.
\tag{43}
\]
This preserves independent and identically distributed preassignment sampling, randomization, the graph law, and anonymous interference.  Moreover,
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\le c/8,\quad
 \|\partial_xg\|_\infty\le3c/4,\quad
 \|\partial_x^2g\|_\infty\le3c,\quad
 \|\partial_x^3g\|_\infty=6c,
\]
which are bounded by \(B,B,B,L\), respectively, by (43).  Hence this alternative remains in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) but is not in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,0}\).  For every \(N_i>0\), exact support correction yields
\[
 \mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}g(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]
 =c\frac{\mathbb E_Z[V_i^4\mathbf1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]}
          {\mu_{2,i}(h)}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
The denominator is positive by \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\), and the numerator is positive because the truncation contains a nearest nonzero exposure-lattice point of positive binomial probability.  Thus the positive-radius class permits a genuine cubic remainder.  Equations (37)--(44) prove every assertion of the proposed statement.

statements.statement:
For the explicit construction in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), all distinct scores over \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) can be represented and computed in polynomial time.  Conditional on \(A\) and the preassignment response functions, for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \leq\overline b_h(A),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \leq\overline s_h(A)^2.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\}\geq1-\alpha\).  If \(C_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A)A\) and
\[
 G_A(C_A)=\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2,
\]
then the explicit bias certificate also satisfies the deterministic bound
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \leq \frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*
      +B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}{n}}.
\]
The exact first two Hoeffding projections create no bandwidth-dependent term.  This result does not assert the sharper uniform rates \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\); the displayed graph norm and conservative variance certificate are the proved computable quantities under the frozen assumptions.
statements.justification: This gives an explicit polynomial-time first-projection PC estimator and a finite-sample conditional certificate without asserting the unproved sharp spectral remainder rates.
statements.gap: The exact first two Hoeffding projections are benign, but the frozen assumptions do not yet yield the edge-restricted projector norm and sharp product-ANOVA bounds needed for a \(d/n\) variance remainder.
statements.consumer: The observable certificate is safe for experiment reporting; its conservative variance term transparently signals that the sharp confidence-length frontier remains unresolved.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(A\), the preassignment response functions, and \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  All expectations and variances below are over the independent coordinates of \(Z\), as specified by \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\).  Put
\[
 X=Z-\frac12\mathbf1_n,\qquad P_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A),\qquad C_A=P_AA,
 \qquad F_h(Z)=\widehat\theta_h.
\tag{1}
\]

We first prove that the corrected variance certificate in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) is valid.  If \(z^{(j)}\) is obtained from \(z\) by flipping coordinate \(j\), the finite maximum defining \(D_{ij,h}\) gives
\[
 |q_{i,h}(z)-q_{i,h}(z^{(j)})|\le D_{ij,h}.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, the left side is zero when \(A_{ij}=0\); when \(A_{ij}=1\), the treated-neighbor count changes from some integer \(m\in\{0,\ldots,N_i-1\}\) to \(m+1\), exactly one of the pairs in that maximum.  The divisions are valid because \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\) gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\) for \(N_i>0\).  Since \(|X_k|=1/2\), the definitions of \(Q_{i,h}\), \(\Gamma_{i,h}\), and \(\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}\) also give, for every assignment,
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)|
 \le Q_{i,h}+2\sum_{j'\in\mathcal V_n}|(C_A)_{ij'}|
 =\Gamma_{i,h},
\tag{3}
\]
and, because flipping \(Z_j\) changes \(X_j\) by one in absolute value,
\[
 |\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)-\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z^{(j)})|
 \le D_{ij,h}+4|(C_A)_{ij}|.
\tag{4}
\]

The response-level part of \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) gives \(|Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)|\le B\).  If \(j=i\), flipping \(Z_j\) changes only the own-treatment argument of unit \(i\), so the response levels differ by at most \(2B\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), then \(j\ne i\), and the neighbor fraction changes by exactly \(N_i^{-1}\); the first-derivative part of \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) and the mean-value identity give a change of at most \(B/N_i\).  If neither condition holds, \({\rm ass:anonymous-interference}\) makes the response unchanged.  Thus, using the zero-denominator convention in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 |Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)-Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z^{(j)})|
 \le B\left\{2\mathbf1\{i=j\}+\frac{A_{ij}}{N_i}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
For real numbers \(g,g',y,y'\), \(|gy-g'y'|\le |g-g'||y|+|g'||y-y'|\).  Applying this identity with (3)--(5) proves
\[
 \left|\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z)Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z)
 -\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}(z^{(j)})Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}(z^{(j)})\right|
 \le\beta_{ij,h}.
\tag{6}
\]
Summing (6) and using \({\rm def:estimator}\) yields
\[
 |F_h(z)-F_h(z^{(j)})|
 \le c_{j,h}:=\frac1n\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}.
\tag{7}
\]

We derive the needed Boolean variance inequality.  Let \(\mathcal F_j=\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_j)\), \(M_j=\mathbb E_Z(F_h\mid\mathcal F_j)\), and \(E_j=M_j-M_{j-1}\), with \(M_0=\mathbb E_ZF_h\).  Conditional centering gives \(\mathbb E_Z(E_j\mid\mathcal F_{j-1})=0\), and hence, for \(j<k\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Z(E_jE_k)
 =\mathbb E_Z\{E_j\mathbb E_Z(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\}=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(F_h)=\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E_ZE_j^2.
\tag{9}
\]
Given \(\mathcal F_{j-1}\), the difference between the two values of \(M_j\) obtained by setting \(Z_j=1\) and \(Z_j=0\) is an average over future coordinates of differences bounded by (7), and is therefore at most \(c_{j,h}\).  Since \(Z_j\) is Bernoulli one half, its conditional variance is at most \(c_{j,h}^2/4\).  Combining this fact with (9), \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), and \({\rm def:radii}\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta_h\mid A,(f_i)_i)
 \le\frac14\sum_jc_{j,h}^2
 =\frac1{4n^2}\sum_j\left(\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}\right)^2
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 =\overline s_h(A)^2.
\tag{10}
\]

We next prove the bias certificate.  For \(N_i>0\), \(q_{i,h}\) depends only on neighbor assignments and is independent of \(Z_i\) by \({\rm ass:bernoulli-design}\).  By \({\rm ass:anonymous-interference}\) and \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\), conditioning first on \(Z_i=a\) and then averaging over its two equiprobable values gives
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 -\frac{\partial_xf_i(1,1/2)+\partial_xf_i(0,1/2)}2\right|
 \le\frac L6h_i(h)^2.
\tag{11}
\]
For \(N_i=0\), \(q_{i,h}=0\), while the derivative part of \({\rm ass:response-envelope}\) bounds the absolute target contribution by \(B\).  Consequently the score part has conditional bias at most
\[
 \frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac Bn\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}.
\tag{12}
\]

It remains to control the PC subtraction.  Centering and \(|Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}|\le B\) imply
\[
 |\mathbb E_Z[X_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]|\le B/2.
\tag{13}
\]
For \(j\ne i\) with \(A_{ij}=1\), condition on all coordinates except \(Z_j\).  The same mean-value argument as in (5), followed by the two-point Bernoulli calculation, gives
\[
 |\mathbb E_Z[X_jY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]|
 =\frac14\left|\mathbb E_Z[Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid Z_j=1]
 -\mathbb E_Z[Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid Z_j=0]\right|
 \le\frac B{4N_i}.
\tag{14}
\]
For \(j\ne i\) with \(A_{ij}=0\), the expectation is zero by anonymous interference and assignment independence.  Equations (13)--(14) imply
\[
 \frac4n\sum_i\left|\sum_j(C_A)_{ij}\mathbb E_Z[X_jY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}]\right|
 \le\frac{2B}{n}\sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|
 +\frac Bn\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|
 =\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (12)--(15) with \({\rm def:target}\), \({\rm def:estimator}\), and \({\rm def:radii}\) proves
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|
 \le\overline b_h(A).
\tag{16}
\]

We also prove the displayed deterministic graph-norm bound.  Because \(P_A\) is a spectral projector of the symmetric matrix \(A\), it commutes with \(A\), and \(C_A=P_AA\) is symmetric.  Write \(C_A=\sum_t\nu_tu_tu_t^\top\) with orthonormal \(u_t\).  Then
\[
 \sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|
 \le\sum_t|\nu_t|\sum_i u_{t,i}^2
 =\sum_t|\nu_t|=\|C_A\|_*.
\tag{17}
\]
For the edge-restricted term, Cauchy--Schwarz within each positive-degree row and then across rows gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|
 &\le\sum_{i:N_i>0}
 \left\{\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}(C_A)_{ij}^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\le\sqrt{nG_A(C_A)}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
Substitution into \({\rm def:pc-handle}\) proves
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
 \le\frac{2B}{n}\|C_A\|_*+B\sqrt{\frac{G_A(C_A)}n}.
\tag{19}
\]

Conditional Chebyshev applied to (10) and (16) yields
\[
 P\!\left(
 |\widehat\theta_h-\theta_n|>
 \overline b_h(A)+\frac{\overline s_h(A)}{\sqrt\alpha}
 \mathrel{\Big|}A,(f_i)_i\right)\le\alpha.
\tag{20}
\]
The derivative envelope and \({\rm def:target}\) give \(|\theta_n|\le B\), so intersection with \([-B,B]\) does not remove the target.  Integrating (20) proves uniform coverage over \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).

Finally, the truncated score for degree \(N_i\) changes only when \(h\) crosses one of at most \(N_i+1\) lattice distances.  Thus all units together create at most \(n^2\) breakpoints.  Exact finite binomial sums compute \(\mu_{2,i}(h)\); the finite maxima compute \(Q_{i,h}\) and \(D_{ij,h}\); one eigendecomposition computes \(C_A\); and matrix and finite-sum arithmetic compute \(\Gamma_{i,h}\), \(\beta_{ij,h}\), and both certificates.  This is polynomial in \(n\).  By \({\rm lem:exact-score-hoeffding-projections}\),
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX,\qquad q_h^{(2)}=0,
\]
so the first projection of \(q_h-4P_AAX\) is \(4(I_n-P_A)AX\) and its second projection is zero, with neither expression depending on \(h\).  The corrected bounded-difference certificate controls all remaining product terms without asserting an unavailable sharp asymptotic order.  This proves every claim.

statements.statement:
Along every triangular-array sequence for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty at every sufficiently large index, \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), and \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) are fixed, there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
At each index the proof fixes the graph primitives of an arbitrary admissible member, retains its kernel \(W\) and the independent \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\) latent types, and changes only the response law.  For almost every \(u\),
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u
 \sim{\rm Binomial}\!\left(n-1,\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv\right),
 \qquad
 \frac{(n-1)\rho_n}{\kappa}
 \leq\mathbb E(N_i\mid U_i=u)
 \leq(n-1)\rho_n\kappa.
\]
These uniform conditional-degree bounds, together with explicit linear, local \(C^3\)-bump, and degree-lattice response pairs, give respectively the graph, interior, and lattice terms for both minimax absolute risk and minimax honest expected length.  No null-row modification or atomic latent-type law is used.
statements.justification: A null-row modification of any admissible integral kernel and an atomic latent-type distribution produce an exact mean-degree \(d\) Erdos--Renyi submodel for every nonempty frozen class; three explicit two-point response experiments then attain all supported-envelope terms.
statements.gap: The positive result uses the literal frozen class, whose latent-type marginal is unrestricted and whose graphon bounds hold almost everywhere; imposing uniform latent types or pointwise graphon constraints would define a different class and would require a new compatibility argument.
statements.consumer: The supported analytic envelope is a global minimax lower benchmark for every nonempty parameter tuple in the frozen model, not only for tuples admitting the equal-block witness.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\neq\varnothing\), and select the graph primitives \(W\), \((\lambda_k,\psi_k)_{k=1}^r\), and the graph sampling law from one member.  We retain those primitives throughout.  All constants below are independent of \(n\) and \(d\), although they may depend on the fixed constants in the theorem.

\textit{Step 1: uniform conditional-degree bounds.}
Define
\[
 w(u)=\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv,
 \qquad
 p_n(u)=\rho_nw(u).
\tag{1}
\]
By \({\rm ass:kernel\text{-}bound}\), \({\rm ass:degree\text{-}regularity}\), and \({\rm ass:edge\text{-}probability}\), there is a Lebesgue-null set \(E\subset[0,1]\) such that, for every \(u\notin E\),
\[
 \kappa^{-1}\leq w(u)\leq\kappa,
 \qquad 0<p_n(u)\leq1.
\tag{2}
\]
The uniform marginal in \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\) gives \(P(U_i\in E)=0\).  Conditional on \(U_i=u\notin E\), the pairs consisting of \(U_j\) and the edge randomizer for \(A_{ij}\), over \(j\neq i\), are independent.  Integrating \({\rm ass:graphon\text{-}draw}\) over the independent \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\) variable \(U_j\) therefore gives
\[
 \Pr(A_{ij}=1\mid U_i=u)
 =\rho_n\int_0^1W(u,v)\,dv=p_n(u),
\tag{3}
\]
and the variables \((A_{ij})_{j\neq i}\) are conditionally independent.  Consequently
\[
 N_i\mid U_i=u\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p_n(u)),
 \qquad
 m_n(u):=\mathbb E(N_i\mid U_i=u)=(n-1)p_n(u).
\tag{4}
\]
Since \(\rho_n=d/n\), (2)--(4) imply
\[
 \frac{(n-1)d}{n\kappa}\leq m_n(u)
 \leq\frac{(n-1)d\kappa}{n}.
\tag{5}
\]
In particular, for \(n\geq2\),
\[
 \frac{d}{2\kappa}\leq m_n(u)\leq\kappa d.
\tag{6}
\]

We record four consequences of (4)--(6).  If \(N\sim{\rm Binomial}(n-1,p)\), expansion of the binomial mass function and the identity \({n-1\choose k}/(k+1)={n\choose k+1}/n\) give
\[
 \mathbb E\frac1{N+1}
 =\frac{1-(1-p)^n}{np}\leq\frac1{np}.
\tag{7}
\]
For \(u\notin E\), (2), (7), and \(N^{-1}\mathbf1\{N>0\}\leq2(N+1)^{-1}\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\left\{N_i^{-1}\mathbf1(N_i>0)\mid U_i=u\right\}
 \leq\frac{2\kappa}{d}.
\tag{8}
\]
Also, (4)--(6) and \(1-x\leq e^{-x}\) give
\[
 \Pr(N_i=0\mid U_i=u)=(1-p_n(u))^{n-1}
 \leq e^{-m_n(u)}\leq e^{-d/(2\kappa)}.
\tag{9}
\]

Conditional on \(A\) and \(N_i=N>0\), \({\rm ass:bernoulli\text{-}design}\) gives \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\), whence
\[
 \mathbb E_Z(V_i^2\mid A,N_i=N)=\frac1{4N}.
\tag{10}
\]
Integrating (10), then using (8), yields
\[
 \mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^nV_i^2\mathbf1\{N_i>0\}
 \leq\frac{n\kappa}{2d}.
\tag{11}
\]

We next bound local exposure mass.  For \(M\sim{\rm Binomial}(N,1/2)\), the maximal atom is bounded by \(C_0N^{-1/2}\).  Indeed, for \(N=2q\), if \(a_q={2q\choose q}4^{-q}\), then
\[
 \frac{a_{q+1}}{a_q}=\frac{2q+1}{2q+2},
 \qquad
 \left(\frac{2q+1}{2q+2}\right)^2\leq\frac{q+1}{q+2},
\tag{12}
\]
so induction gives \(a_q\leq(q+1)^{-1/2}\); an odd-binomial central atom is bounded by an adjacent even central atom.  The event \(|M/N-1/2|\leq h\) contains at most \(2Nh+2\) lattice points.  Hence
\[
 \Pr\{|M/N-1/2|\leq h\mid N\}
 \leq C_1\{\sqrt N\,h+N^{-1/2}\}.
\tag{13}
\]
For a binomial variable with mean \(m\), exponential Markov's inequality at \(t=\log2\) gives
\[
 \Pr(N<m/2)
 \leq e^{tm/2}(1-p+pe^{-t})^{n-1}
 \leq\exp\{-c_0m\},
 \qquad c_0=(1-\log2)/2>0.
\tag{14}
\]
Splitting according to \(N_i\geq m_n(U_i)/2\), and using (6), (14), and \(d\to\infty\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E\{N_i^{-1/2}\mathbf1(N_i>0)\}
 \leq C_2d^{-1/2}.
\tag{15}
\]
Jensen's inequality and (6) also give
\[
 \mathbb E\sqrt{N_i}\leq\sqrt{\mathbb EN_i}\leq\sqrt{\kappa d}.
\tag{16}
\]
Combining (13), (15), and (16), and using \(h\geq d^{-1}\) from \({\rm def:bandwidth\text{-}set}\), we obtain uniformly for \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\),
\[
 \Pr(|V_i|\leq h,N_i>0)
 \leq C_3\{\sqrt d\,h+d^{-1/2}\}
 \leq2C_3\sqrt d\,h.
\tag{17}
\]

Finally choose \(K>e\kappa\) so large that
\[
 a_K:=K\log\{K/(e\kappa)\}>2/C_{\log},
 \qquad D_n=\lceil Kd\rceil.
\tag{18}
\]
The binomial Chernoff bound obtained by optimizing exponential Markov's inequality, together with \(m_n(u)\leq\kappa d\), gives
\[
 \Pr(N_i>D_n\mid U_i=u)
 \leq\left\{\frac{e m_n(u)}{D_n}\right\}^{D_n}
 \leq e^{-a_Kd}.
\tag{19}
\]
No independence among the degrees is needed for the union bound.  By \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\max_{1\leq i\leq n}N_i>D_n\right)
 \leq ne^{-a_Kd}
 \leq n^{1-a_KC_{\log}}=o(1).
\tag{20}
\]

\textit{Step 2: response submodels and a common distance bound.}
Let \(s_0=B/4\), and let \((\xi_i)_{i=1}^n\), independently of \((U,A,Z)\), be independent with density
\[
 p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2s_0}\right)
 \mathbf1\{|t|\leq s_0\}.
\tag{21}
\]
The substitution \(y=\pi t/(2s_0)\) verifies that (21) integrates to one.  For a deterministic \(g\in C^3[0,1]\), define
\[
 f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x),
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in[0,1].
\tag{22}
\]
If
\[
 \|g\|_\infty\leq3B/4,
 \qquad
 \max_{1\leq j\leq2}\|g^{(j)}\|_\infty\leq B,
 \qquad
 \|g^{(3)}\|_\infty\leq L,
\tag{23}
\]
then (21)--(23) verify \({\rm ass:response\text{-}envelope}\) and \({\rm ass:third\text{-}derivative\text{-}bound}\).  Moreover, \((U_i,f_i^\pm)\) are independent and identically distributed, and their \(U_i\)-marginal remains \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).  Thus \({\rm ass:unit\text{-}sampling}\) holds; the retained graph primitives satisfy every graph condition of \({\rm def:model\text{-}class}\), and \({\rm ass:anonymous\text{-}interference}\) defines the potential outcomes.  Each sign in (22) therefore produces a law in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  By \({\rm def:target}\),
\[
 \theta_n^\pm=\pm g'(1/2),
 \qquad
 \Delta_g:=|\theta_n^+-\theta_n^-|=2|g'(1/2)|.
\tag{24}
\]

Let \(q_{s_0}=\sqrt{p_{s_0}}\), extended by zero outside \([-s_0,s_0]\).  The cosine vanishes at the endpoints, so \(q_{s_0}\) is absolutely continuous, and direct integration gives
\[
 \|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2=\frac{\pi^2}{4s_0^2}.
\tag{25}
\]
For translations \(\eta_1,\eta_2\), the fundamental theorem of calculus followed by Minkowski's integral inequality gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H^2\{p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1),p_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\}
 &=\|q_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_1)-q_{s_0}(\mathord\cdot-\eta_2)\|_2^2\\
 &\leq(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2\|q_{s_0}'\|_2^2
 =\frac{\pi^2(\eta_1-\eta_2)^2}{4s_0^2}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
Here \(H^2(p,q)=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\).  Define the observed neighbor fraction
\[
 X_i=\begin{cases}1/2+V_i,&N_i>0,\\0,&N_i=0.\end{cases}
\tag{27}
\]
Conditional on \((A,Z)\), the outcomes under (22) are independent translates of (21), and the two translations for unit \(i\) differ by \(2g(X_i)\).  Hellinger affinity multiplies for product laws.  Since \(H^2=2(1-\text{affinity})\) and \(1-\prod_i(1-x_i)\leq\sum_i x_i\) for \(0\leq x_i\leq1\), (26), followed by averaging over the common \((A,Z)\) marginal, gives
\[
 H^2(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq\frac{\pi^2}{s_0^2}\mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^ng(X_i)^2.
\tag{28}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p-q|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_g^+,Q_g^-)
 \leq H(Q_g^+,Q_g^-).
\tag{29}
\]

\textit{Step 3: the linear graph-floor pair.}
Let
\[
 g_G(x)=c_GB\sqrt{d/n}\,(x-1/2).
\tag{30}
\]
Because \({\rm ass:sparse\text{-}limit}\) gives \(d/n\to0\), condition (23) holds for all sufficiently large \(n\) whenever \(0<c_G\leq1\).  Equations (9), (11), (27), and (30) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\sum_{i=1}^ng_G(X_i)^2
 &=c_G^2B^2\frac dn
 \left\{\mathbb E\sum_iV_i^2\mathbf1(N_i>0)
 +\frac n4\Pr(N_i=0)\right\}\\
 &\leq c_G^2B^2
 \left\{\frac\kappa2+\frac d4e^{-d/(2\kappa)}\right\}
 \leq C_4c_G^2B^2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
Put
\[
 \eta=(1-2\alpha)/2>0.
\tag{32}
\]
Since \(s_0=B/4\), (28), (29), and (31) permit a fixed choice of \(c_G>0\) for which
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_G^+,Q_G^-)\leq\eta.
\tag{33}
\]
Equation (24) gives the target separation
\[
 \Delta_G=2c_GB\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{34}
\]

\textit{Step 4: the local \(C^3\)-bump pair.}
Suppose \(L>0\), and define
\[
 \phi(t)=t(1-4t^2)^4\mathbf1\{|t|<1/2\}.
\tag{35}
\]
The fourth-order zeros at the endpoints make the zero extension a \(C^3(\mathbb R)\) function, and \(\phi'(0)=1\).  Put \(C_j=\|\phi^{(j)}\|_\infty\), \(0\leq j\leq3\), and, for \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), let
\[
 g_h(x)=c_ILh^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{h}\right).
\tag{36}
\]
Then
\[
 \|g_h^{(j)}\|_\infty=c_ILh^{3-j}C_j,
 \qquad 0\leq j\leq3.
\tag{37}
\]
Choose \(c_IC_3\leq1\).  Since \({\rm ass:log\text{-}degree}\) implies \(d\to\infty\) and \(h\leq d^{-1/2}\), (37) verifies (23) for every sufficiently large \(n\).  The bump vanishes at the isolate exposure \(0\), and its nonzero support is contained in \(|V_i|\leq h\).  Therefore (17), (28), and (36) give
\[
 H^2(Q_h^+,Q_h^-)
 \leq C_5c_I^2n\sqrt d\,L^2h^7.
\tag{38}
\]
Let
\[
 h_0=\{L^{-2}/(n\sqrt d)\}^{1/7}.
\tag{39}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), substitution of (39) into (38), and a fixed further decrease of \(c_I\), give
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{h_0}^+,Q_{h_0}^-)\leq\eta.
\tag{40}
\]
By (24), (35), and (36),
\[
 \Delta_I=2c_ILh_0^2
 =2c_IL^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{41}
\]

\textit{Step 5: the degree-lattice pair.}
Continue to suppose \(L>0\).  With \(D_n\) from (18), put \(w_n=(4D_n)^{-1}\) and
\[
 g_D(x)=c_DLw_n^3\phi\!\left(\frac{x-1/2}{w_n}\right),
 \qquad c_DC_3\leq1.
\tag{42}
\]
Because \(D_n\to\infty\), the analogue of (37) verifies (23) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(1\leq N_i\leq D_n\), every noncentral exposure point satisfies
\[
 |V_i|\geq
 \begin{cases}N_i^{-1},&N_i\text{ is even},\\(2N_i)^{-1},&N_i\text{ is odd},\end{cases}
 \geq(2D_n)^{-1}>w_n.
\tag{43}
\]
At a central point, oddness of \(\phi\) gives \(g_D(1/2)=0\), and at an isolate \(g_D(0)=0\).  Hence, on \(F_n=\{\max_iN_i\leq D_n\}\), the complete observed outcomes under both signs in (22) equal \(\xi_i\).  The two data laws agree on \(F_n\), while the event has the same probability under both laws.  Thus (20) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_D^+,Q_D^-)
 \leq\Pr(F_n^c)=o(1)\leq\eta
\tag{44}
\]
for every sufficiently large \(n\).  From (24), (35), and (42),
\[
 \Delta_D=2c_DLw_n^2\asymp Ld^{-2},
\tag{45}
\]
where the comparison constants depend only on the fixed \(K\).

\textit{Step 6: risk and honest-length reductions.}
For any one of the preceding pairs, write its target values as \(\theta^+,\theta^-\), its data laws as \(Q^+,Q^-\), and its separation as \(\Delta\).  For an arbitrary estimator \(T\), define \(A_T=\{|T-\theta^+|\geq\Delta/2\}\).  On \(A_T^c\), the triangle inequality gives \(|T-\theta^-|\geq\Delta/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}|T-\theta^+|+\mathbb E_{Q^-}|T-\theta^-|
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{Q^+(A_T)+Q^-(A_T^c)\}\\
 &\geq\frac\Delta2\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{46}
\]
If the total variation is at most \(\eta\), the larger risk is at least \(\Delta(1-\eta)/4\).

Let \(\mathcal C\) be any interval-valued procedure admissible in the honest-length criterion of \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\).  Uniform coverage and the definition of total variation imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q^+\{\theta^+,\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}
 &\geq Q^+\{\theta^+\in\mathcal C\}
      +Q^+\{\theta^-\in\mathcal C\}-1\\
 &\geq(1-\alpha)+(1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q^+,Q^-))-1\\
 &\geq1-2\alpha-\eta=(1-2\alpha)/2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
An interval containing both target values has length at least \(\Delta\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q^+}\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C)
 \geq\Delta(1-2\alpha)/2.
\tag{48}
\]
Taking the infima in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\), (33)--(34), (40)--(41), and (44)--(45) show that each minimax criterion is bounded below, up to fixed positive constants, by \(\sqrt{d/n}\), by \(L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}\) in the interior regime, and by \(Ld^{-2}\), respectively.

\textit{Step 7: comparison with the supported envelope.}
Set \(a_n=(n\sqrt d)^{-1/2}\).  For \(L>0\), (39) gives
\[
 Lh_0^2=a_nh_0^{-3/2}=L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{49}
\]
If \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), then \(L^2\geq d^{13/2}/n\), and hence \(a_nd^{3/2}\leq Ld^{-2}\).  Evaluation at \(h=d^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2Ld^{-2}.
\tag{50}
\]
If \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), evaluation at \(h_0\) and (49) gives
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}.
\tag{51}
\]
If \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\), then \(L^2\leq d^3/n\), so \(Ld^{-1}\leq\sqrt{d/n}\); at \(h=d^{-1/2}\), the stochastic term also equals \(\sqrt{d/n}\).  Therefore
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+a_nh^{-3/2}\}
 \leq2\sqrt{d/n}.
\tag{52}
\]
When \(L=0\), the infimum is attained at \(d^{-1/2}\) and equals \(\sqrt{d/n}\).

In the regime of (50), combine the graph and lattice pairs; in the regime of (51), combine the graph and interior pairs; in the regime of (52), or when \(L=0\), use the graph pair.  If a nonnegative criterion is at least \(c_1x\) and at least \(c_2y\), it is at least \(\min(c_1,c_2)(x+y)/2\).  Equations (34), (41), (45), and (50)--(52) therefore give a fixed \(c>0\) such that
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\left[\sqrt{d/n}+
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}\{Lh^2+(n\sqrt d\,h^3)^{-1/2}\}\right].
\tag{53}
\]
The same argument using (48) gives (53) with \(R^*_{n,d,L}\) replaced by \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\).  The bracket is \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) by \({\rm def:frontier\text{-}envelope}\).  Every constructed response law preserves the selected member's kernel and independent uniform latent types.  Divisions by \(B\), \(d\), and \(N_i\) are legitimate because \(B>0\), \(d>0\), and the factor \(N_i^{-1}\) is used only on \(\{N_i>0\}\); Steps 4--5 are invoked only when \(L>0\).  This proves both inequalities and the final construction claims.

Conditionally on \(A\), write \(X_j=Z_j-1/2\), \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)^\top\), and \(q_h=(q_{1,h},\ldots,q_{n,h})^\top\).  For a centered scalar function \(g(X)\), define its first projection as \(g^{(1)}=\sum_j\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]\) and its second projection as
\[
 g^{(2)}=\sum_{j<k}\left\{\mathbb E[g\mid X_j,X_k]
 -\mathbb E[g\mid X_j]-\mathbb E[g\mid X_k]\right\},
\]
and apply these definitions coordinatewise to a vector.  The first two conditional Hoeffding projections of the exact-support score satisfy
\[
 q_h^{(1)}=4AX,\qquad q_h^{(2)}=0
\]
simultaneously for every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\).  Consequently, for every \(A\)-measurable orthogonal projector \(\Pi\),
\[
 \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(1)}=4(I_n-\Pi)AX,
 \qquad \{(I_n-\Pi)q_h\}^{(2)}=0,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\!\left[\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2\mid A\right]
 =4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(i\) and condition on \(A\).  If \(A_{ij}=1\), the \(N_i\) neighbor contrasts are exchangeable.  By \({\rm lem:exact-score-moments}\) and \(V_i=N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}X_k\),
\[
 1=\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]
 =N_i^{-1}\sum_{k:A_{ik}=1}\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_k\mid A]
 =\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}X_j\mid A].
\]
If \(A_{ij}=0\), then \(q_{i,h}\) is independent of the centered variable \(X_j\), so the same expectation is zero.  Since \(\mathbb E_ZX_j^2=1/4\), the orthogonal projection of \(q_{i,h}\) onto the span of \(X_j\) is \(4A_{ij}X_j\).  Summing over \(j\) proves \(q_h^{(1)}=4AX\), uniformly in \(h\).

For the second projection, the simultaneous sign reversal of all neighbor contrasts sends \(V_i\) to \(-V_i\), hence sends the odd score \(q_{i,h}\) to \(-q_{i,h}\).  For distinct \(j,k\), integrate over all contrasts except \((X_j,X_k)\).  The resulting function on \(\{-1/2,1/2\}^2\) is odd under \((X_j,X_k)\mapsto(-X_j,-X_k)\).  Its Walsh expansion therefore contains only the two degree-one monomials and no constant or degree-two monomial.  After subtraction of the first projections, the \(\{j,k\}\) interaction is zero.  This proves \(q_h^{(2)}=0\).

An \(A\)-measurable linear map preserves Hoeffding order, proving the two displayed identities with \(I_n-\Pi\).  Finally, conditional independence and \(\mathbb E_Z[XX^\top\mid A]=I_n/4\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_Z\|4(I_n-\Pi)AX\|_2^2
 =16\operatorname{tr}\!\left((I_n-\Pi)AA^\top(I_n-\Pi)\frac{I_n}{4}\right)
 =4\|(I_n-\Pi)A\|_{\mathrm F}^2,
\]
where symmetry of \(A\) and idempotence of \(I_n-\Pi\) justify the last equality.

Let \(I_0(A)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\).  Under the repaired class, any graph-only radius \(b(A)\) that is required to satisfy
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_Z(\widetilde\theta-\theta_n\mid A,(f_i)_i)\right|\leq b(A)
\]
for every response configuration in the conditional support must obey
\[
 b(A)\geq \frac{B}{n}I_0(A)
\]
on every realized graph.  Whenever \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\) is nonempty, the independent-Rademacher response submodel \(f_i(a,x)=\varepsilon_iBx\) is admissible, and even a genie revealing every nonisolate sign leaves, conditionally on \(A\), Bayes absolute-error risk between
\[
 \frac{B}{\sqrt3\,n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \frac{B}{n}\sqrt{I_0(A)}.
\]
Thus the corresponding unconditional missing-sign fluctuation is of order \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\), which is no larger than the expected conditional radius \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\).  This distinction neither constructs an unconditionally honest interval nor proves that every such interval must pay the graph-only conditional radius.
statements.justification: Opposite derivative signs on realized isolates give identical conditional observed laws, while an independent-sign calculation gives the exact square-root-count unconditional fluctuation scale.
statements.gap: The first conclusion is conditional on the graph and response configuration; it does not establish a sharp expected length for all unconditionally honest procedures.
statements.consumer: Analysts using the conditional certificate must retain the realized isolate allowance or explicitly change the inferential conditioning convention.

sampling_model.units: One triangular-array population with independent preassignment draws \((U_i,f_i)\); the finite-population derivative is realized after this draw.
sampling_model.network: One observed undirected graph drawn conditionally independently from the sparse finite-rank graphon \(\rho_nW\), with \(\rho_n=d/n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Own treatment is independent of the neighbor count conditional on the preassignment graph.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is known and fixed at one half; each positive realized degree uses its exact nearest nonzero exposure support, and isolates remain explicitly unsupported.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Graphon eigenfunctions are replaced by the leading empirical eigenspace; leave-one-edge-out residualization returns observable bias and variance remainder certificates.
sampling_model.inference_randomness: Coverage and risk average over the declared preassignment unit draw, graph draw, and Bernoulli assignment, as in the retained model; graph-observable radii expose the realized support contribution.

tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the new finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, the graph dependence term, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit frontier retains lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. A same-class testing calculation gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates, whereas the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\); therefore no full matched-frontier theorem is claimed. The open content is uniform feasible-PC certification and tail-adaptive completion without minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions. Li and Wager's Theorem 6 is used only through an explicit finite-to-derivative bridge as an asymptotic benchmark.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a degree-exact, bias-aware statistical frontier for a causal derivative from one network, with observable support diagnostics and an honest distinction between conservative isolate bias and the same-class testing modulus.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.

technical_internal_limitation: For \(N_i>0\), the exact score has second moment \(\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\) and third-order bias at most \(Lh_i(h)^2/6\). These identities do not establish the feasible spectral remainders. Isolates have no exposure variation, so the safe interval adds their full derivative envelope. Under i.i.d. preassignment responses, the corresponding same-class testing modulus is smaller, of order \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\); closing that upper--lower gap requires an estimator, not a stronger assumption.
honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is only an asymptotic benchmark after \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\). Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius; isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a proposed matching converse, and the same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus is explicit. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(B\pi_{0,n}\) upper allowance is not matched by the \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) isolate testing term. The open tail-adaptive construction must retain the i.i.d. \((U_i,f_i)\) class and the stated conditioning convention. Unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside scope.
